topLevel.why: Y mostly preserves separate stories and major divisions, whereas X repeatedly combines independently headed works and even places Liberation Spectrum inside Human Readable. Y has some unnecessary fragmentation, particularly separating Epoch's title and advertisement from its narrative, but its divisions are substantially more faithful.

gists.why: Y has a slight advantage in passage-specific guidance, especially for the office visit and BIGMAC's hardware dependence, although X better describes Lawrence's recollection and the legal negotiation. Both have mismatches, and Y adds an unsupported discrimination claim to Gretl's funding history.

weldedParts.why: Combines the title, contents, publication history, and editorial notes with the separately headed introduction.
Combines The Right Book and Other People's Money, two separately headed stories with their own afterwords.
Combines Human Readable and its afterword with the distinct story Liberation Spectrum and its afterword.
Combines Visit the Sins, Constitutional Crisis, and Pester Power, which the document presents as separate stories.

weldedParts.part: Vats, AIs, and the Business of Writing
weldedParts.why: Combines Chicken Little, Epoch, their afterwords, and Russell Galen's separately headed essay.

inventedClaims.what: Attributes Gretl's unsuccessful funding attempts to her gender and age; the passage describes an investor dismissing her business because it would not scale.

overall.why: Y provides a much more reliable map of the collection's individual works and generally more localized reading guidance. Its occasional overfragmentation and gist errors are less disruptive than X's extensive merging of separate stories.
